applicable_when: The kernel is a pure layout-transpose (no compute): it reads a (128,64,3,3) tensor in NCHW row-major order and writes it in a permuted stride layout. The current tile config XBLOCK=128 with xnumel=9 wastes 119 of 128 threads every cycle (only 9 x-elements exist). This produces only 0.48 waves across 132 SMs, leaving 64% of the GPU idle. The MemoryCacheAccessPattern rule confirms 18/32 bytes per sector are wasted due to the stride mismatch. Adding @triton.autotune with configs that use small XBLOCK (matching xnumel=9 -> 16) and large YBLOCK (to fill more SMs) will dramatically increase grid size, occupancy, and memory coalescing efficiency.
